Computing
Our Computing lessons at Nyewood are all about technology. Here are some links that explain what computers and the internet are and how we can use some of their features. Make sure you look at them with an adult.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zymykqt
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zbhgjxs
In our Computing lessons we begin to learn about programing, algorithms and codes. Here are some videos and games to support your learning! Make sure you watch and play them with an adult.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/z3tbwmn
https://www.j2e.com/j2code/
https://blockly.games/?lang=en
https://www.lightbot.com/flash.html
We also begin to use laptops and computers so it is important to know how to use a keyboard. Here are some games to help. Make sure you play them with an adult.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zf2f9j6/articles/z3c6tfr
http://www.bigbrownbear.co.uk/freetyping/
https://www.arcademics.com/games/sky-chase
https://www.arcademics.com/games/typing-jets
Perhaps you could ask your adults if you can type some words or write a story once you have practised.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years - Nyewood CE Infant School
pageCache.text:
Early Years
At Nyewood Infant School in Early Years we understand the importance of children exploring their learning through play. This play and exploration can be enhanced through well used resources. Here you will find some links to different internet resources which we hope can help you.
Maths
Here are some websites which can help support everyday mathematical learning and language.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zjkphbk/articles/zd4b382
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/znyyscw/articles/zkgp6v4
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zhsspg8/articles/zfqcbdm
Topmarks Maths Games - https://www.topmarks.co.uk/maths-games/5-7-years/counting
ICT Games (Maths) - http://www.ictgames.co.uk/
Communication Language and Literacy (including reading and writing)
Here is an app which you might like to download (free on smart phones), it will help you take stories wherever you go,
https://www.bbc.co.uk/cbeebies/watch/storytime-app
Here is a programme which can help support the early learning of phonics,
Alphablocks - https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episode/p0872x41/alphablocks-magic-words-1-meet-alphablock-a
At Nyewood Infant School we often use Phonics Play in both our taught sessions and during the children’s choosing time. At home you could find it helpful as it has a range of games to play from early learners to later stages in phonics learning.
Phonics Play - https://www.phonicsplay.co.uk/resources
Oxford Owl - https://home.oxfordowl.co.uk/kids-activities/learning-activities-age-5/
Teach Your Monster to Read - https://www.teachyourmonstertoread.com/teachers-area/classroom-toolkit/phonics-songs
ICT Games (English) - http://www.ictgames.co.uk/
Understanding the World
This part of our curriculum is all about looking and exploring the world around us. Please take time to stop and talk about things you see and the changes around you. Talk about previous trips both in the UK and abroad, what was similar and what was different.
Here are a few programmes and games which are good at exploring different parts of the world and how things work.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/cbeebies/shows/do-you-know
https://www.bbc.co.uk/teach/class-clips-video/eyfs-ks1-geography-go-jetters/zj8ypg8
http://resources.hwb.wales.gov.uk/VTC/animal_homes/eng/Introduction/default.htm
Throughout the year, Cbeebies publish a range of videos, quizzes and activities linked to learning about other cultures and traditions such as Chinese New Year, St George’s Day and the festival of Eid. To find these, head to their site and enter the festival into their search engine:
https://www.bbc.co.uk/cbeebies/topics
This area of the curriculum also explores technology and how things move or work. Here are some websites which can support this learning without having to use any resources;
https://www.terrapinlogo.com/emu/beebot.html
Expressive Arts and Design
This area of our curriculum explores making marks, creating but also listening, making and moving to music.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/cbeebies/shows/bitz-and-bob
https://www.bbc.co.uk/cbeebies/curations/mister-maker-makes
Here is an App which you might like to look at (free)
https://www.bbc.co.uk/cbeebies/watch/cbeebies-get-creative-app
https://www.bbc.co.uk/teach/bring-the-noise/eyfs-ks1-music-play-it-bring-the-noise/z4sq92p
Physical Education
Like many things in our curriculum we believe that its best that you just get up and get going. Don’t forget if and when you have time to join in with your children as it makes their learning more memorable.
Supermovers - https://www.bbc.co.uk/teach/supermovers
Body Coach - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uqLNxJe4L2I
Jump Start Jonny - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CD5Xa4Zt4Zc
Physical Education is not just about keeping active. It is also about teaching our children to live a healthy lifestyle. The following websites may help you to discuss these ideas with you child
Diet - http://resources.hwb.wales.gov.uk/VTC/2010-11/foundation-phase/fph-2/index.html

pageCache.text:
Humanities
At Nyewood, our Humanities lessons are split between History and Geography.
In History, we talk about the past and about different significant people in the past. We look at the special things they did and why they were important. We talk about our own pasts and how things change during our lives. We also get to look at special objects from the past!
This year we are learning about a special nurse who helped poorly people in the past. Take a look at this video about her. Remember to ask an adult first: https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zns9nrd/articles/znsct39
In Geography we learn about where we live and all about God’s world. We talk about the different places in the UK and the seasons. We find out about the oceans and where different countries are. We talk about the temperature and why it is hot in some places and cold in others. Take a look at this game to find out more about the world. Make sure you ask an adult first.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/games/embed/education-ivor-pirate-rabbits?exitGameUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fbbc.co.uk%2Fbitesize%2Farticles%2Fz6vyf4j
You can explore the UK more here: https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zyhp34j/articles/z4v3jhv
You can explore France here: https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zyhp34j/articles/zhw7vk7
Maybe you would like to learn about Nigeria in Africa: https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zyhp34j/articles/znxp92p

pageCache.text:
Mathematics
Mathematics at Nyewood is all about numbers, shapes and measures. We want everyone to have a sense of number. This means we can think about how is best to solve a problem rather than just learning facts, although knowing some facts will make things easier.
At home there is maths all around you.
Maybe you can help with the cooking, reading recipes and weighing or counting out ingredients.
You might want to learn how to tell the time by reading a clock so you know when it is dinner or bedtime.
Counting things around the house is also a great activity. You might want to count socks or shoes in twos or gloves in fives.
Perhaps you might have some loose change in the house somewhere. Can you name the coins? Maybe you would like to play shops with it and the other people in your house to help you add and take away.
Playing board games with a dice will help your counting on and recognising dice patterns without needing to count.
There are also lots of good games you can play on your computer or tablet too. Make sure you play them with an adult, so you are safe, and so they know you are not playing games too easy or hard for you.

pageCache.text:
PE
Our PE lessons at Nyewood are all about physical health and wellbeing. Here are some links that explain why physical health and wellbeing are so important to us. Make sure you look at them with an adult.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/clips/z274d2p
https://www.gosh.nhs.uk/medical-information/general-health-advice/leading-active-lifestyle/exercise-children-and-young-people
Children in primary schools are required to be active for 60 minutes a day. Here are some great websites including videos and ideas of ways of keeping active at home.
https://www.nhs.uk/change4life
https://www.bbc.co.uk/teach/supermovers
https://www.gonoodle.com/
https://www.activekidsdobetter.co.uk/active-home
In our PE lessons, we develop children’s fundamental movement skills such as agility, balance and coordination. In EYFS, children develop their gross motor skills in a range of ways such as creating obstacle courses, exploring with different ways of moving (running, jumping, balancing etc) and much more. Children in EYFS also develop their fine motor skills as part of their physical development, such as mark marking with different media, and activities known as ‘funky fingers’. In addition to this, children are taught about their hygiene and health in relation to physical development. Here are some examples of the types of activities that you could complete at home:
In KS1, children’s fundamental movement skills such as agility, balance and coordination are taught creatively through the teaching of gymnastics, dance, games and agility and fitness lessons. Here are some links to support your learning.
https://www.tes.com/teaching-resource/ks1-dance-warm-up-video-11931684
https://primarypeplanning.com/home-pe-ks1-challenge-activities/

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education - Nyewood CE Infant School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
Our RE (Religious Education) lessons at Nyewood are learning about Christianity and the life and teachings of Jesus through stories from the Bible and learning about other faiths and celebrations, such as Judaism.
The first story we learn from the Bible is about Creation. This clip is useful to demonstrate the idea of God as the creator of everything. Which of these things made them feel happy, amazed, sad or worried. Why? If they had the power to create something, what would that be? Why?
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/clips/z62hyrd
Next, we learn about Noah’s Ark. Watch the clip with an adult and ask some questions about the story.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qzYjy6lhRag
We are learning about other faiths in the world. We are learning about Judaism. Watch the clip and discuss what is the same and what is different from your home.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/clips/zd9jxnb
At Easter time we learn about the Easter Story.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/clips/zjgkq6f
Ask your child 'Why do Christians call such a sad day Good Friday?' This clip explains this question. How do you celebrate Easter?
At Christmas time we learn about the Christmas Story.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/clips/zntfgk7
How do you celebrate Christmas with your family? Do you go to Church? Do you see your family? Draw what Christmas looks like for you.

Science
Science at Nyewood is practical and focuses on the world around us. Children will be learning about the importance of asking questions, gathering evidence, carrying out experiments and looking at different ways of presenting their results.
The BBC has a great section covering the science we will be exploring:
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/subjects/z6svr82
Explorify at home suggests science activities for parents and carers. It's based on the primary science curriculum, but easy to do at home with no special materials needed:
https://explorify.wellcome.ac.uk/blog/explorify-during-school-closures
Crickweb has some fun games to play based on the science we will be looking at:
http://www.crickweb.co.uk/ks1science.html

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club - Nyewood CE Infant School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club is run Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 9:00 am. We charge £4.50 per session which is paid in advance via the Arbor App. Please see the office for details of how to sign up.
Children may be dropped off from 8:00 am at the White Hall gate (accessed via the playground). Parents or carers must accompany their child to the gate and personally hand them over to a member of the club staff.
All children will be offered breakfast, with a range of healthy options including cereal and toast. Breakfast is a relaxed, sociable time where children sit together in small groups around a table. After eating, there is a short period for children to relax and enjoy quiet games and activities before the school day begins.
At 9:00 am, children will be taken directly from Breakfast Club to their classrooms, ready for the start of the school day.

pageCache.text:
Governors
Our Vision: Smiling, Caring and Learning Together on a Journey with God.
Our Mission: To deliver high quality learning experiences which enable children to develop their personal capabilities to the full allowing them to take an active role in God’s world.
To deliver the best possible teaching and learning through a curriculum and learning environment that is safe, exciting, creative and fun. By fostering an understanding of the teaching of Jesus, in accordance with the beliefs and traditions of the Church of England, we seek to develop in our children an understanding of their own uniqueness and spirituality.
Our Ethos: The school aims to serve its community by providing an education of the highest quality within the context of Christian belief and practice. It encourages an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith and promotes Christian values through the experience it offers all its pupils.
Recognising its historic foundation, the school will preserve and develop its religious character in accordance with the principles of the Church of England and in partnership with the Church at parish and diocesan level.
Strategic Direction: The path we follow in adopting strategies, objectives and goals in order to deliver our vision and mission.
Strategies, Objectives and Goals: Are both corporate and individual. Corporately they are set out in the School Development Plan and monitored by the school self-evaluation processes; individually they are set out and monitored via the performance management processes.
Please contact the Governing Body via [email protected] addressing David Mobsby.

pageCache.pageTitle: Treehouse Club - Nyewood CE Infant School
pageCache.text:
Treehouse Club
Our Wraparound Care provision is split into two parts. From 3:10 until 4:00 we have a club, listed below are all the activities we complete throughout the week. The second part is our Treehouse which runs from 4:00 until 5:30, this time is more relaxed for the children to chose their activities from a wide variety of games as well as having a substantial snack before they are collected.
Monday to Friday, 3:10pm until 4:00pm - £5 per session.
Afterschool Clubs can be booked directly through the Arbor App. Limited spaces are available for each club and these are on a first come first served basis.
In Woodland Club, children connect with nature through outdoor learning and exploration. Activities include bug hunts, den building, and learning about local plants and wildlife.
Get outside and get moving! Join us for fast-paced games, fun challenges and tons of outdoor action. Make friends, try new activities and enjoy the fresh air every week!
Build, create and imagine at our Lego Club where kids can design amazing structures, tackle fun building challenges and let their creativity soar.
Dive into a world of squishy, splashy fun at our Messy Play Club – where kids can explore textures, colours and creativity through hands on sensory activities.
Creative Crafts will inspire children to design, build and create using a variety of materials. Each week brings a new project to develop creatively! We will be problem-solving and using our artistic skills to make wonderful creations out of a variety of materials.
Children will go straight from their classrooms at the end of the school day to their club.
Parents can collect their child any time up until 5.30pm on Monday to Friday. Children need to be collected from Holly Class door, ring the doorbell located on the green gate just past the office.
Treehouse costs £7.50 per session, this included access to a range of relaxing and fun toys, games and activities for children to engage with as well as being offered a substantial snack and drink such a sandwich or wrap.

pageCache.pageTitle: Learning Zone - Nyewood CE Infant School
pageCache.text:
Learning Zone
When we use the internet and this learning zone we need to make sure we use it safely. There are some rules to follow that you will have learnt about in school…
Ask an adult before you use technology;
Tell an adult if you see something that makes you sad or that you don’t know;
Keep your personal information a secret;
Don’t talk to strangers.
Here are some videos that you can watch to remind you of how to keep safe online.
https://www.thinkuknow.co.uk/4_7/
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zfcvhbk/articles/zkcj92p
https://www.saferinternet.org.uk/advice-centre/young-people/resources-3-11s
https://www.childnet.com/resources/smartie-the-penguin
https://www.childnet.com/resources/digiduck-stories
